notes: Characters now remember properly. Rather than three hardcoded patterns — your name, something you like, what you do — a pass after every couple of messages reads the exchange and writes down whatever is worth still knowing months from now: your work, health, the people around you, plans, and the things the two of you did or promised each other. The store holds four hundred of these per character instead of a handful. Recall is the bigger change: what gets sent used to be the most recent dozen, which meant a fortnight of small talk pushed the thing that mattered off the end. Now the last few messages are read for what they are about, and matching memories are pulled back from anywhere in the store — mention the motorway drive you were dreading and the memory of you dreading it comes back, however long ago you said it. Pinned memories still always go, and you can write and pin your own from the memories screen. Two fixes underneath: near-identical facts were being swallowed by an over-eager duplicate check that compared text as substrings, so a note ending in 19 could vanish because one ending in 1 already existed; and the rolling conversation summary was compressing hard enough to lose names, dates and exact promises, which was where the specifics were going.
